_provenance.source_title: DC Council pending & proposed street-safety legislation
_provenance.source_agency: DC Council via the Legislative Information Management System (LIMS)
_provenance.source_description: Bills introduced or pending in the current Council period that bear on street safety. Deliberately SEPARATE from data/legislation.json (enacted law), whose validator requires a code.dccouncil.gov URL. Pending bills live in LIMS and change status frequently, so every entry carries a freshness date and an explicit status-verification flag.
_provenance.methodology: Seed inventory drawn from PLAN.md Workstream D1 (advocacy-campaign references as of 2026-07). Bill numbers, statuses, committee assignments, and hearing dates are NOT yet re-confirmed against LIMS in this pass — each entry is flagged status_verified:false until a bounded LIMS lookup confirms it. Do not present any status as fact until verified.
caveats: Statuses shown are advocacy-campaign references, not LIMS-confirmed as of capture. Every card is marked 'status unverified' until a LIMS lookup confirms bill number, committee, and hearing dates.
Pending bills expire at the end of a Council period if not enacted; a bill listed here may have been reintroduced under a new number.
This surface tracks legislative intent, not delivery — an introduced bill is a proposal, not a promise kept.
Nothing here should be cited as enacted law; enacted mandates live in the Safe Streets Law Tracker (legislation.json), sourced to the D.C. Law Library.

bills.title: Motor Vehicle Insurance Modernization
bills.summary: Raises crash-victim insurance minimums so people injured or killed by drivers are less likely to face catastrophic uncovered costs.
bills.status_note: Named as an active DC Families for Safe Streets campaign as of 2026-07 with a pre-assembled coalition (WABA, DC FSS, DC PAC, MADD, DC Multimodal Accessibility Council, Institute for Safer Trucking, Truck Safety Coalition, BAC). Confirm bill number, committee, and hearing schedule in LIMS.

bills.title: Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) expansion
bills.summary: Expand Intelligent Speed Assistance beyond STEER's repeat-offender program toward broader deployment. Advocacy handle: #StopSuperSpeeders.
bills.status_note: Active DC Families for Safe Streets campaign as of 2026-07. Bill number not yet identified — run a bounded LIMS search for the current ISA-expansion vehicle before presenting a number.

bills.title: Automated-enforcement revenue designation follow-through
bills.summary: Any active successor measure ensuring automated-enforcement (camera) revenue is designated to safety programs, building on D.C. Law 24-321 / § 50-921.20.
bills.status_note: Placeholder for a successor/oversight measure to the enacted ATE Revenue Designation. Confirm whether a live bill exists in Council Period 26 via LIMS; if none, keep as an oversight watch item, not a bill.

lineage.label: Ten-year arc of DC street-safety law
lineage.note: The legislative lineage this project's accountability work sits on. Enacted entries link to the Safe Streets Law Tracker; earlier entries are listed for context and are flagged where their exact citation still needs verification.

entries.core_promise: Established DC's Vision Zero commitment to eliminate traffic fatalities and serious injuries.

entries.short_title: Bicycle and Pedestrian Safety Amendment Act of 2016
entries.core_promise: Strengthened protections for people biking and walking, including contributory-negligence and safety-infrastructure provisions.

entries.short_title: Vision Zero Enhancement Omnibus Amendment Act of 2020
entries.core_promise: Top-15 dangerous-corridor safety reporting, 20 mph local/collector speed limits, right-on-red restrictions near sensitive uses.

entries.short_title: Safe Streets for Students Amendment Act of 2022
entries.core_promise: School-zone safety measures: School Streets pilots, 15 mph zones, school-safety action plans.
Right-on-red and daylighting-style protections advancing pedestrian safety at intersections.
Designated automated-enforcement revenue toward safety purposes.
Repeat-speeder accountability, including an Intelligent Speed Assistance program for the most dangerous drivers.
